content.content:
#### Virtualized

The list is virtualized: however many tasks the project has run, it lays out and draws only the rows in view, and a few rows either side of it, never every row, so opening the tab, scrolling it, resizing the sidebar, filtering, and new tasks arriving cost the same with ten thousand previous tasks as with ten. Every row is 28 pixels tall, group headings and a chain's expanded steps included, so where each row lies is known from its place in the list alone, without laying out the rows before it, and the scrollbar's thumb is sized and placed from the whole list's height, as though every row were drawn.
A row is drawn only from what its row shows, its mode, status, first line, and time, read from each task's history record once and kept, never by reading a record's output, lines, or snapshots while scrolling; those are read only when a task is opened. Running rows update their time and spinner in place, redrawing only what is in view. Scrolling to a row, as when the tab opens on Running, a filter changes, or a queued row is dragged past the edge, jumps straight to its place without drawing the rows between. A row scrolled out of view and back is the same as it was, its chain expanded or not, its selection and highlight kept.
Scrolling past either end does nothing: with the list at its top or its bottom, a wheel, trackpad, or drag that goes further leaves every row exactly where it is, frame after frame, with no stretch, bounce, or nudge of even a pixel and back, and draws nothing anew, since nothing moved. Its scroll position is clamped to its ends before a frame is drawn, never drawn past an end and corrected the frame after, and kept in whole device pixels, so a row never shimmers between two places. What lies at an end stays at it: a running row's time ticking, a task finishing, a row added or removed elsewhere in the list, or the tab being resized never makes the rows in view jump and settle. A list scrolled to its bottom stays at its bottom as rows are added, and one at its top stays at its top. The list counts as taller than the tab only once it overflows it by a whole pixel, as the right sidebar's panels do, so a list that fits never scrolls at all.

#### Details
61:A panel whose contents fit doesn't scroll at all, not even by a pixel, at any display scale or window size: it counts as taller than its contents need only once they overflow it by a whole pixel or more, so what is left over from rounding to the display's pixels never counts, and while they fit, it stays scrolled to its top. So neither the wheel nor a drag moves rows that all fit, and no scrollbar shows for them.

content.text:
The Tasks tab list should no longer flicker when you're already scrolled to its top or bottom. I couldn't watch it in the real app, so the flicker fix isn't checked on screen; the new test of the clamping math and all existing tests pass.

The cause was that a wheel or trackpad scroll moved the list past its end. The rows were then laid out from that overshot position and pulled back a frame later, which is the flicker you saw.

The fix, in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`:

- **Held at the ends before drawing:** each frame, the scroll position is clamped to the list's ends before any rows are chosen or drawn, so nothing is ever drawn past an end.
- **Whole pixels:** the position is rounded to whole device pixels so rows don't shimmer between two places.
- **Scrolling further at an end is ignored:** at the top or bottom, a scroll that would go further is stopped before the list takes it. Nothing moves and nothing is redrawn.
